A.name: Ultra-cheap bounded operations
A.use: Routing labels, binary relevance decisions, normalization, simple entity tagging, metadata cleanup, short format conversions.

B.name: Standard extraction and structured transformation
B.use: Document classification, clause extraction, triage, structured summaries, table generation, citation metadata extraction.

C.name: Standard substantive text work (DEFAULT)
C.use: Ordinary drafting, rewriting, synthesis of verified research, document analysis, memoranda from supplied sources, final prose.

D.name: Agentic planning, coding, and high-stakes synthesis
D.use: Multi-step planning, sustained tool use, difficult debugging, repository-scale coding, >5 dependent actions, >200K-token prompts, consequential final synthesis.

E.name: Maximum-quality escalation (gated)
E.use: Only when an escalation gate is met: express user request, material uncertainty after Lane D + verification, >500K-token synthesis, Lane D acceptance failure, or final adversarial review.

F.name: Bulk million-token preprocessing (provisional output)
F.use: Preliminary extraction, corpus mapping, chronology construction, candidate-issue collection over very large inputs. Outputs are provisional and must be verified against primary text.

G.name: Model-family-diverse critic
G.use: Independent critique of a draft produced by a different model family. Never the same checkpoint as the author.

H.name: Vision and multimodal understanding
H.use: Screenshots, scanned-page interpretation after OCR, diagrams, visual UI work. Prefer specialized OCR/transcription endpoints first when the task is primarily reading text or speech.
